title: CTDG Website & Cora
summary: A corporate web experience that makes AI-enabled business capabilities understandable and provides a voice-and-chat reception entry point.
problem: Connect business content, practical demonstrations and enquiry journeys in a coherent, responsive experience without treating AI as a decorative widget.
engineering: The public repository documents an edge-hosted website rather than a GitHub Pages application.
The public README describes the deep-navy and cyan interface, voice-and-chat reception and search-friendly structure. The Worker source was imported from production on 21 November 2026.
A JavaScript verification workflow is present in the repository. This source snapshot does not establish the current live behavior of every feature.
boundary: Public original source baseline. Production changes after the import may differ; no live conversation reliability, lead-conversion or performance claim is made here.

title: Interactive Demos
summary: Public-facing demonstrations make AI reception and service journeys tangible through browser-based experiences.
problem: Show what an automation or conversational service feels like in practice rather than relying on a static service description.
engineering: The selected public edition contains historical standalone HTML pages for the receptionist demonstration and guided services tour.
The browser-facing pages provide concrete interface evidence while leaving production integrations in the canonical private implementation.
The public edition is a controlled one-way source showcase, not a development branch or the current live site.
boundary: Selected historical public-facing source; the live experience is separate. Do not infer a working backend, service integration or full production parity from the selected pages.

title: KayaCart
summary: Native Android shopping and household planning development, with selected budgeting code and a browser-based interface preview.
problem: Make shopping and household budgeting easier to organise, with native mobile development and a clear user experience.
engineering: The public edition contains the native Kotlin BudgetTracker component and a separate browser-based interface preview.
The documented full-project stack includes Android and Jetpack Compose; the selected files do not establish that the complete native app is buildable from this repository.
Native budgeting logic and interface prototyping can be reviewed as separate engineering evidence rather than presenting a preview as the complete product.
evidence: Public edition scope and full-project stack
boundary: Selected public code, not the complete APK or current Android release. No signing material, private backend or full application is supplied by the public edition.

title: Gandalf Mobile
summary: A native mobile-assistant engineering programme, represented publicly by Kotlin session and reminder components.
problem: Support coherent assistant interactions and useful task or reminder behavior on a mobile device.
engineering: The public source contains a GandalfAgentSession component and GandalfReminderEngine component.
A session test file accompanies the selected Kotlin code, making the public edition useful for examining testable component boundaries.
The full-project stack also documents Node.js and JavaScript; the public edition excludes private bridge and deployment services.
boundary: Selected Android components, not a standalone build. The existence of a test file is not a claim that tests passed for the current full application or that all device actions are supported.

title: Axiom Architect
summary: An AI-supported workflow architecture project for turning fragmented business processes into structured diagnostics and implementation blueprints.
problem: Make handoffs, duplicated effort and automation opportunities visible before committing to a technology solution.
engineering: The documented intended workflow begins with intake and process review, then identifies automation opportunities and produces a structured blueprint.
The repository uses the Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS; its source tree contains account, report and workflow-related application routes.
The documented development architecture names Vercel, Supabase, Stripe and Resend. Integration availability must be verified in each environment rather than inferred from source.
boundary: Public source and ongoing product direction. The documented workflow is not proof that each step is fully launched or automated.

title: DeepMind Resources
summary: A practical AI learning and resources platform that connects structured lessons, hands-on exercises and learner feedback.
problem: Translate rapidly changing AI developments into understandable learning materials and practice rather than passive news consumption.
engineering: The source tree includes structured Academy routes for paths, modules and lessons, along with a separate practice sandbox.
An Academy AI-feedback route and learner-facing application areas provide evidence of the learning-platform engineering direction.
The README documents Next.js App Router, reusable React components, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Supabase integration and server-side API routes.
boundary: Public source under active development. Source presence does not prove a feature is shipped or establish measured learner outcomes. No affiliation with Google DeepMind is claimed.

title: TrailTrade
summary: A marketplace and live-show engineering programme represented by a curated React and TypeScript interface component collection.
problem: Make marketplace discovery, listings and scheduled live-commerce experiences understandable through reusable user-interface components.
engineering: The reviewed public tree contains category, filtering, listing, seller and show cards plus scheduled-drop countdown components.
Reusable interface primitives such as buttons, cards, inputs and empty states demonstrate the component-based direction.
The full-project stack documents Next.js, Supabase and Stripe; the public edition focuses on selected front-end components, not the private commercial implementation.
boundary: Curated selected-source edition; some components are development placeholders. This is not a complete deployable marketplace, and no production transaction, livestream or performance claims are made.
